title: SUDER: Self-Improving Unified Large Multimodal Models for Understanding and Generation with Dual Self-rewards

problem.claim: Large multimodal models struggle with accurate vision-language alignment, including contradictions between generated text and visual input and failures to follow text-to-image prompts.

gap.claim: Existing solutions require external supervision and address only one direction of the understanding-generation task pair.

contributions.claim: SUDER is a framework that reinforces multimodal understanding and generation using a self-supervised dual reward mechanism.
The framework uses the duality between understanding and generation to provide self-supervised optimization signals for each task from the other.
For an input, SUDER samples multiple outputs in one task domain, reverses the input-output pairs, and computes dual likelihood within the model as self-rewards for optimization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on visual understanding and generation benchmarks.
The authors report that SUDER improves model performance without external supervision, with especially notable improvements in text-to-image tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large multimodal models unify cross-model understanding and generation.
These models remain vulnerable to vision-language misalignment and prompt-following failures.
Existing approaches depend on external supervision and handle only one task direction.
SUDER treats understanding and generation as inverse dual tasks and trains them with dual self-rewards computed from reversed sampled pairs.
The authors report benchmark improvements without external supervision, particularly for text-to-image tasks.

source_observation.claim: Understanding and generation are presented as naturally inverse dual tasks that can provide optimization signals for one another.

interpretation.claim: A model's paired task capabilities may be used as mutual self-supervision when the task relationship supports reversible evaluation.

application.claim: For related inverse tasks, consider generating outputs in one direction and evaluating reversed pairs with an internal likelihood-based reward.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported visual understanding and generation benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the specific benchmarks, datasets, or baseline models.
Quantitative results and statistical significance are not reported.
Training details, computational cost, and failure cases are not described.
